body.proof_tex:
The conditional coverage proof (12)--(16) depends only on polynomial reproduction, Holder bias, bounded unit clusters, the two full-design centering restrictions, cross-unit independence, donor independence, the donor fourth-moment calculation, ellipticity, and the upper local modulus.  Every one of these premises holds in the iid subclass, and \(C_{\alpha,\mathrm{iid}}\) uses exactly the same radii and fallback computed from its own weights.  Replacing each selected beta bandwidth by \(h_s^{\mathrm{iid}}\) in (12)--(16) therefore proves exact finite-sample coverage.

For expected length, the deterministic event and historical radii remain \(O(R_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2})\).  The iid selector moment with exponent \(\lambda\) gives
\[
\mathbb E[A_L^{\mathrm{iid}}\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good,iid}}\mid E_0]
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{sm}}^{1/2}+T^{-\lambda/d}+N^{-\lambda/2}\},
\]
and the unchanged donor allowance is \(O(N^{-\kappa/2})\).  The iid bad-event probability is \(O(R_\star)\), so the fallback contributes \(O(R_\star)\le O(R_\star^{1/2})\).  Hence the expected length is at most \(CR_\star^{1/2}\).

Finally, apply the overlap argument (18) to the iid pairs in \texttt{lem:iid-joint-law-embedding}.  Their fixed perturbation constants can be decreased so that affinity exceeds \(2\alpha+a_0\) while target separation remains a fixed multiple of the square root of the appropriate channel rate.  Maximizing over four channels under strict slack and three at equality proves the lower brackets.  The \(\epsilon\)-slack argument from (18) gives the same result for uniformly asymptotically honest intervals.
body.justification: The iid-tuned interval retains exact conditional coverage and attains the no-log honest-length rate.
